meta.title: Clean-Room Reimplementations
meta.tagline: Open-source projects that rebuild closed software from the ground up
meta.intro: A curated index of clean-room reimplementations: projects that rebuild a specific closed-source product — an application, a game engine, a network protocol, an operating system — from scratch, rather than wrapping or forking the original. Every entry names the product being reimplemented and the language it is written in. Nothing here is a mirror or a repackaging.
meta.disclaimer: Compiled from public sources — no independent testing of the linked projects. Star counts were read from the GitHub API on 2026-10-17 and drift daily. A high star count reflects attention, not correctness or completeness: several projects here are early and explicitly unfinished.

sections.title: Applications
sections.description: Desktop software rebuilt from scratch. This group is currently dominated by a wave of Rust rewrites that each target one widely-used commercial application.

items.name: PhotoCraft
items.what: A photo editor written from scratch to stand in for Adobe Photoshop, including layered editing and non-destructive adjustment.

items.name: PdfCraft
items.what: A PDF reader and editor reimplemented in place of Acrobat, covering viewing, annotation and page manipulation.

items.name: FilmCraft
items.what: A non-linear video editor written to fill the role of Adobe Premiere, with a timeline and render pipeline of its own.

items.name: WordCraft
items.what: A word processor reimplemented to cover the Microsoft Word feature set, including layout and document formatting.

items.name: LightCraft
items.what: A non-destructive photo editor targeting the Lightroom workflow: cataloguing, develop settings and batch processing.

items.name: VectorCraft
items.what: A vector art tool rebuilt in place of Adobe Illustrator, with paths, anchors and scalable editing.

items.name: EffectCraft
items.what: Motion graphics and compositing written from scratch as an alternative to After Effects.

items.name: GridCraft
items.what: A spreadsheet reimplemented along the lines of Microsoft Excel, covering formulas and cell-model editing.

items.name: CadCraft
items.what: Computer-aided design and drafting rebuilt as a standalone application, targeting the AutoCAD working model.

items.name: DeckCraft
items.what: A presentation and slideshow tool reimplemented in place of PowerPoint, with slide layout and sequencing.

items.name: SoundCraft
items.what: A digital audio workstation rebuilt to occupy the Pro Tools niche: multitrack recording, editing and mixing.

items.name: FigCraft
items.what: Interface design and prototyping reimplemented as an alternative to Figma, covering frames, components and layout.

items.name: paper-rs
items.what: A native Rust infinite-canvas design app, also aiming at the Figma use case, built on egui and wgpu rather than a web stack.

items.name: System7
items.what: An open-source reimplementation of Apple Macintosh System 7, including the classic desktop and window manager.

sections.title: Games and engines
sections.description: The oldest and most established corner of the practice: game engines and services rebuilt from reverse-engineered behaviour or published specifications, usually because the original is abandoned or the servers are gone.

items.name: SanAndreasUnity
items.what: An open-source reimplementation of the GTA: San Andreas engine in Unity, loading the original game assets into a new runtime.

items.name: Impostor
items.what: A reimplementation of the Among Us server, letting players host their own games after the official matchmaking changed.

items.name: Jazz² Resurrection
items.what: An open-source reimplementation of Jazz Jackrabbit 2, including the original level formats and game logic.

items.name: KisakCOD
items.what: An open-source reimplementation of the Call of Duty 4 engine, assembled from leaked and reverse-engineered sources.

items.name: donut
items.what: An open-source reimplementation of The Simpsons: Hit & Run, targeting the original game's engine behaviour.

items.name: Chariot
items.what: A cross-platform reimplementation of the Age of Empires engine, written in Rust.

items.name: Abyss Engine
items.what: A clean-room reimplementation of the Diablo 2 engine, written in C with its own asset pipeline.

items.name: FreeHL
items.what: A clean-room reimplementation of Half-Life deathmatch and its game logic, built on the FreeCS codebase.

items.name: OpenBattlefield2
items.what: A clean-room reimplementation of DICE's Refractor 2 engine, the technology behind Battlefield 2.

items.name: openDoJa
items.what: A desktop-focused clean-room reimplementation of DoJa, the Java-based mobile platform used by early Japanese phones.

sections.title: Services, runtimes and platforms
sections.description: Not applications but infrastructure: protocols, servers, hardware runtimes and shells rebuilt so they can run without the vendor.

items.name: usque
items.what: An open-source reimplementation of the Cloudflare WARP client, speaking the same protocol without the proprietary client.

items.name: OpenTPU
items.what: An open-source reimplementation of Google's Tensor Processing Unit, reproduced from the published ISA documentation.

items.name: Pash
items.what: An open-source reimplementation of Windows PowerShell for Mono and .NET, so scripts can run off Windows. Archived upstream.

items.name: LuxonServer
items.what: A clean-room reimplementation of the Photon LoadBalancing server, the matchmaking layer many Unity games depend on.

items.name: libdragon
items.what: An open-source SDK for the Nintendo 64, built by reverse-engineering the official development libraries. Archived upstream; superseded by the community fork.
